text:
S-104's next ship date is **PO005791, 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80 NF, low-peroxide), promised for 2026-10-07**. If that shipment slips, the customers exposed are the ones buying the **cyclosporine eye-emulsion line: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL, and the cyclosporine 0.05% generic**. That's 13,986 prescriptions (TRx) in the last 13 weeks. Eight health systems account for about 77% of that volume.

The risk is real for three reasons:
- **No backup supplier.** S-104 is the only qualified supplier for RM-221. The listed alternate, S-131, is not qualified.
- **Second single-source step.** RM-221 then goes into an emulsifier premix (CMP-310) that only S-201 makes.
- **Poor on-time record.** 32.3% of S-104's closed purchase orders shipped late.

**Recovery time:** once RM-221 finally arrives, it takes about **50 days** to get Lacrivia 5 mL to the distribution centre. That covers 6 days transit, 10 days for the premix, 12 days across two bulk-emulsion steps, 3 days filling, and 19 days for final QC release (including a 14-day sterility test) plus 4 days transit to the DC. Every day of supplier delay pushes availability back by the same amount.

**Affected products**
| Product | NDC | Through | TRx, last 13 weeks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL | 99101-0101-05 | RM-221 (single source) | 7,017 |
| Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL | 99101-0101-10 | RM-221 | 3,425 |
| Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL | 99101-0202-05 | RM-221 | 3,544 |
| Lens-care solutions 1–11 | 99101-4001…4011 | RM-221 | Not in the commercial database |
| *Oculon 2.5 mL / 5 mL* | *99101-0303-25 / -50* | *RM-222* | *2,568 / 986* |

The Oculon rows are a lower risk: RM-222's next order is due later (2026-10-26) and has a qualified backup supplier (S-130). I left Oculon out of the rankings below.

The approved substitute for Lacrivia is the cyclosporine 0.05% generic, but it depends on the same failing supply chain. **There is no usable substitute.**

**Sources and definitions**
- **Next ship date:** the earliest promised ship date on S-104's open orders (supply purchase-order table).
- **Late-ship rate:** the ratified metric (closed orders shipped late ÷ all closed orders).
- **Single source:** the ratified qualified-supplier count (= 1).
- **Products exposed:** traced through the current bill of materials only, using the supply-exposure trace. Superseded BOM links and the deprecated BOM_FLAT_LEGACY table were not used.
- **Recovery time:** standard manufacturing times from get_lead_times, following the recovery lead-time rule (BR-LEAD-01).
- **Customer and payer volume:** follows the approved product-to-customers-and-payers path. Prescriptions come from the weekly 3rd-party TRx table (RXT_WKLY), linked through each prescriber's account, with payers from the plan-to-payer lookup (PAYER_SPINE). The last 13 weeks run from 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-25.
- **"Customer":** the top-level account under rule BR-CUST-01. Clinics are rolled up to their health system; independent clinics count on their own.
- **Contract tiers and allocation:** tiers come from the governed supply_contracts reference list; allocation order is BR-ALLOC-01; the substitute check is BR-SUB-01.
- **Policy:** no restrictions apply to these tables for the supply-planner role. The incentive-compensation goals table was not used.

**Assumptions**
- "Misses its next ship date" means the 2026-10-07 RM-221 order slips. The other two open orders (RM-221 on 10-29, RM-222 on 10-26) would make the exposure worse.
- The 50-day recovery time is for Lacrivia 5 mL. The other cyclosporine packs take a similar route.
- Lens-care products have no prescription data, so there is no customer view for them here.

                      AND (toLower(n.name) = toLower(nm) OR n.id = nm)
                    RETURN n LIMIT 1
                    UNION
                    MATCH (n:Table) WHERE toUpper(n.fq_name) = toUpper(nm) OR toUpper(n.fq_name) ENDS WITH '.' + toUpper(nm)
                    RETURN n LIMIT 1 }
                  MERGE (d)-[:USED]->(n) RETURN collect(DISTINCT coalesce(n.fq_name, n.name)) AS linked

question: Which customers are exposed if supplier S-104 misses its next ship date? Show the affected products and the top 10 accounts and payers by volume on them.
answer:
S-104's next ship date is **PO005791, 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80 NF, low-peroxide), promised for 2026-10-07**. If that shipment slips, the customers exposed are the ones buying the **cyclosporine eye-emulsion line: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL, and the cyclosporine 0.05% generic**. That's 13,986 prescriptions (TRx) in the last 13 weeks. Eight health systems account for about 77% of that volume.

The risk is real for three reasons:
- **No backup supplier.** S-104 is the only qualified supplier for RM-221. The listed alternate, S-131, is not qualified.
- **Second single-source step.** RM-221 then goes into an emulsifier premix (CMP-310) that only S-201 makes.
- **Poor on-time record.** 32.3% of S-104's closed purchase orders shipped late.

**Recovery time:** once RM-221 finally arrives, it takes about **50 days** to get Lacrivia 5 mL to the distribution centre. That covers 6 days transit, 10 days for the premix, 12 days across two bulk-emulsion steps, 3 days filling, and 19 days for final QC release (including a 14-day sterility test) plus 4 days transit to the DC. Every day of supplier delay pushes availability back by the same amount.

**Affected products**
| Product | NDC | Through | TRx, last 13 weeks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL | 99101-0101-05 | RM-221 (single source) | 7,017 |
| Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL | 99101-0101-10 | RM-221 | 3,425 |
| Cyclosporine 0.05% 5 mL | 99101-0202-05 | RM-221 | 3,544 |
| Lens-care solutions 1–11 | 99101-4001…4011 | RM-221 | Not in the commercial database |
| *Oculon 2.5 mL / 5 mL* | *99101-0303-25 / -50* | *RM-222* | *2,568 / 986* |

The Oculon rows are a lower risk: RM-222's next order is due later (2026-10-26) and has a qualified backup supplier (S-130). I left Oculon out of the rankings below.

The approved substitute for Lacrivia is the cyclosporine 0.05% generic, but it depends on the same failing supply chain. **There is no usable substitute.**

If stock runs short, the shortage allocation rule ships to Tier A first (#1–3), then Tier B (#4 and #7), then everyone else in proportion to their last-13-week TRx.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Next ship date:** the earliest promised ship date on S-104's open orders (supply purchase-order table).
- **Late-ship rate:** the ratified metric (closed orders shipped late ÷ all closed orders).
- **Single source:** the ratified qualified-supplier count (= 1).
- **Products exposed:** traced through the current bill of materials only, using the supply-exposure trace. Superseded BOM links and the deprecated BOM_FLAT_LEGACY table were not used.
- **Recovery time:** standard manufacturing times from get_lead_times, following the recovery lead-time rule (BR-LEAD-01).
- **Customer and payer volume:** follows the approved product-to-customers-and-payers path. Prescriptions come from the weekly 3rd-party TRx table (RXT_WKLY), linked through each prescriber's account, with payers from the plan-to-payer lookup (PAYER_SPINE). The last 13 weeks run from 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-25.
- **"Customer":** the top-level account under rule BR-CUST-01. Clinics are rolled up to their health system; independent clinics count on their own.
- **Contract tiers and allocation:** tiers come from the governed supply_contracts reference list; allocation order is BR-ALLOC-01; the substitute check is BR-SUB-01.
- **Policy:** no restrictions apply to these tables for the supply-planner role. The incentive-compensation goals table was not used.

**Assumptions**
- "Misses its next ship date" means the 2026-10-07 RM-221 order slips. The other two open orders (RM-221 on 10-29, RM-222 on 10-26) would make the exposure worse.
- The 50-day recovery time is for Lacrivia 5 mL. The other cyclosporine packs take a similar route.
- Lens-care products have no prescription data, so there is no customer view for them here.
